title: Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet

topics.title: Earth as a unique planet among the planets of the solar system

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how all life on Earth exists in a very thin layer at its surface.
Classify the eight planets as small rocky planets or large planets made mostly of gases.
Explain why Venus is the hottest planet and how the greenhouse effect differs from a plant greenhouse.

topics.title: Position of the Earth and the habitable zone

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Earth's distance from the Sun lets water stay liquid and define the habitable zone.
State why the Earth looks blue from space.
Describe what scientists know and think about the possibility of life on Mars.

topics.title: Size of the Earth, its orbit and the ozone layer

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Earth's nearly circular orbit keeps sunlight and heat steady through the year.
Explain how the Earth's size and gravity allow it to hold an atmosphere without crushing life.
Describe how the ozone layer protects living cells from ultraviolet rays.
State that the Earth behaves like a giant magnet with a magnetic field.
Distinguish cosmic rays from the solar wind and explain why these particles are harmful.
Explain how the magnetic field shields the atmosphere and life on Earth.

topics.title: Earth systems that sustain life and the importance of balance

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the atmosphere, hydrosphere, geosphere and biosphere and what each contains.
Define geodiversity and explain how it creates varied habitats.
Analyse how a change in one part of the Earth system affects other parts.

topics.title: Continuity of life and asexual reproduction

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how reproduction and genes keep each kind of organism continuing and allow change.
Describe asexual reproduction in microbes and simple animals and why offspring are copies.
Give examples of plants that grow from leaf, stem or root parts.

topics.title: Sexual reproduction in plants and animals

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the role of gametes and why offspring of two parents differ from each other.
Describe pollination, fertilisation and the formation of seeds and fruits in flowering plants.
Compare fertilisation and embryo development in fish and frogs, birds and mammals.
Name the three challenges that make up the triple planetary crisis.
Explain how burning fossil fuels causes global warming and climate change and its effects.
Describe global agreements and everyday actions that help protect the environment.
